_comment: A 2D-periodic slab: Li metal under LiFSI/EC/DMC electrolyte, 468 atoms.
THE LABELS ARE UMA MLIP PREDICTIONS, NOT DFT, and the energy includes a
harmonic wall above z = 30.285 A in the ORIGINAL cell. This example
teaches the settings a slab needs; it is not a reference-quality
workflow and the numbers it reaches mean nothing about accuracy.
The two settings below are a PAIR. `pbc` marks z as the open axis;
interaction between the slab and its periodic images across the
vacuum. slab_correction without exactly one false entry in pbc is
refused at construction, and a false entry without the correction
Padding the cell is NOT a substitute. A dipolar interface keeps
interacting with its images however much vacuum you add, and the
error barely shrinks. Padding stops the DESCRIPTOR seeing across
the gap; the correction stops the ELECTROSTATICS doing so.
mesh_dimensions follows the PADDED cell, 14.04 x 14.04 x 52:
ceil(14.04/1.25) = 12 and ceil(52/1.25) = 42. Using the original
32.285 would under-resolve the reciprocal sum along z.

loss._comment: No virial labels in this trajectory, so its prefactors stay 0.

training._comment: 468 atoms, so one frame per step. 34 frames is far too few for a real model -- see the README.
